The graph shows the number of cell phone subscriptions per capita for the whole world.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
phones <- readr::read_csv("../www/cell-phone-penetration.csv") |>
  dplyr::mutate(rate = subscribers / population)
phones |>
  gf_point(rate ~ year) |>
  gf_line() |>
  gf_labs(y = "subscriptions per capita")
```

Find sensible values for the input and output-scaling parameters using hillside() to represent the relationship between per capita subscriptions and year.

$$ \text{subscriptions}(\text{year})) \equiv A\, \text{hillside}\left(a (\text{year} - b)\right) + B$$

1. What are the input scaling parameters?

```{mcq}
#| label: cbs-1-wlc
#| inline: true
1. A & a
2. B & b
3. A & B
4. a & b [correct]
```

2. Which of these is the best value for B (with units subscribers per capita) to align the function with the data?

```{mcq}
#| label: cbs-2-yw3
#| inline: true
1. -0.15
2. 0
3. 0.15
4. 0.25
```

3. Which of these is the best value for A?

```{mcq}
#| label: cbs-3-ydux
#| inline: true
1. -1.1
2. 0.9
3. 1.1 [correct]
4. 1.5
```

4. Which of these is the right set of units for A?

```{mcq}
#| label: cbs-4-xjc
#| inline: true
1. people
2. people per capita
3. subscribers
4. subscribers per capita [correct]
```

5. Which of these is the best value for b (with units of years)?

```{mcq}
#| label: cbs-5-dke
#| inline: true
1. 2004.5
2. 2007.5 [correct]
3. 2009.5
4. 2011.5
```

6. Which of these is a sensible value for a?

```{mcq}
#| label: cbs-6-dke
#| inline: true
1. 5 years
2. 5 per year
3. 21 years
4. 21 per year
```

:::
